title: Paint with Copper's Four Colors
lead: Copper slowly changes from shiny orange to blue-green. Pick the colors you like, then wax them so they stay.

steps.title: Meet the four stages
steps.text: Copper has four stages. New copper turns Exposed, then Weathered, then Oxidized. These four blocks are waxed, so they will never change.

steps.title: Build in new copper
steps.text: Here is a little tower made of new copper. The walls are Cut Copper. The windows are Copper Grates.

steps.title: Wait, and it all turns green
steps.text: Leave copper alone and it ages by itself, bit by bit. Rain does not speed it up. Covering it does not stop it.

steps.title: Mix the stages on purpose
steps.text: Now use the stages like paint. Keep the walls orange, and make the corners green. Let the roof get greener near the top. Then wax every block.

steps.title: Add copper details
steps.text: Finish with a Lightning Rod on top and Copper Lanterns by the door. Copper Lanterns burn with a green flame.

body: To wax copper, use a honeycomb on it. Waxed copper looks the same as plain copper. Check the name: it starts with Waxed.
Changed your mind? Use an axe. The first scrape takes off the wax. Each scrape after that takes away one stage.
Copper looks extra good in Vibrant Visuals. Metal blocks like copper reflect sunlight and the glow of lights.
tips: Shear a full bee nest or beehive to get 3 honeycomb. Put a lit campfire under it first, so the bees stay calm.
Wax keeps it as it is
Wax stops copper from changing. It does not turn green copper orange again. Scrape first, then wax.
A lit Copper Bulb gets dimmer as it ages. Its light level goes 15, 12, 8, then 4. Wax it to keep it bright.
When lightning hits copper that is not waxed, it wipes away all the green.
challenge: Build a well with a copper roof. Make it fade from orange at the bottom to green at the top. Wax it when it looks just right.
